description:
"Houston, we have a story to tell."

Years ago, bold explorers set out to "Dare Mighty Things," leaving historic rovers and landers on the Moon and Mars. Today, those machines sit in silent dust. Our team is here to bring their forgotten stories back to life.
summary:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten: Echoes of Pasadena is an illustrated digital comic book created solo by an A-Level student for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Designed for young learners and space enthusiasts, the comic transforms dense NASA and Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) archives into a culturally rooted story connecting the past, present, and future of space exploration.
The story centers on a debate between a grandfather, Hichcha, and his young grandson, Appuhami, about astronomy and satellites. Stepping in as a mediator, a Professor—who was once Hichcha's Sinhala student—bridges cultural heritage with modern space science. He explains how JPL engineers in Pasadena carried human culture into outer space through probes and rovers, and how the discoveries of silent spacecraft from the past continue to guide the present and inspire the future.
This project is important because it shows that space exploration is a continuous human journey. By blending intergenerational Sri Lankan storytelling with verified NASA data, it ensures our silent off-world explorers are never forgotten.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten: Echoes of Pasadena is an interactive, voiced digital comic book created solo by an A-Level student for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Designed for school-age learners and casual space enthusiasts, the comic translates complex technical records from NASA and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) into a multimedia storytelling experience.

The story follows a lively generational debate between a grandfather named Hichcha (a former Sinhala teacher) and his curious grandson, Appuhami, about astronomy and satellites. A Professor—who was once Hichcha's Sinhala student—steps in as a mediator to guide both the characters and the readers through space history. Together, they explore how NASA's isolated rovers, landers, and deep-space probes—such as Voyager 1 and the Mars Rovers—have played a major role in carrying humankind's knowledge, culture, and legacy toward interstellar space.

Interactive Features & Multimedia Experience:

  • Original Voice Acting: Readers can listen to the characters speak—with Grandfather Hichcha and young Appuhami voiced directly by the creator—bringing warmth and emotion to the comic panels.
  • Direct Educational Links: Embedded links throughout the comic direct readers straight to official NASA websites and mission archives to explore real spacecraft data, images, and discoveries further.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Dense engineering archives often discourage young students from exploring space history. By combining hand-drawn visuals, character voices, and clickable NASA resources, this project makes space science engaging and accessible. Its intended impact is to spark STEM curiosity among young learners, honor the engineers behind historic missions, and show how humanity's isolated spacecraft paved the road to interstellar exploration.

How It Is Creative:
The entire concept, storyline, and hand-drawn artwork are original creations by a solo student creator. Blending local Sri Lankan intergenerational storytelling with audio narration and interactive NASA web links transforms a traditional comic into an immersive bridge between human culture and deep space.

Tools & Software Used:

  • Microsoft Paint (MS Paint): Used to draw the original comic characters and scenes by hand.
  • Canva: Used for comic panel assembly, audio voice integration, interactive link embedding, layout formatting, and digital publishing.
  • Google AI & Canva AI: Used strictly for grammar checking, text formatting refinement, and basic image cleanup.
  • Official Data & Reference Imagery: Sourced from NASA and NASA/JPL open archives.
